name: PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi)
short_description: Direct income support of ₹6,000 per year to landholding farmer families.
description: A central government income-support scheme launched in 2019 that transfers cash directly into the bank accounts of eligible landholding farmer families across India, in three equal instalments, to help meet input costs for crop production and household needs.
benefits: ₹6,000 per year per family, paid in 3 instalments of ₹2,000 every four months, transferred directly to the farmer's bank account (DBT).
eligibility: Farmer family must hold cultivable agricultural land in their name
Certain categories are excluded, such as institutional landholders and some high-income or professional categories (see official guidelines)
Land size is not the primary criterion after the 2019 expansion — most landholding families qualify
land_size_info: Open to landholding farmer families of any size, subject to exclusion criteria for certain non-farming or high-income categories.
irrigation_info: Not a deciding factor for this scheme.
application_process: Register online on the PM-KISAN portal, or visit your local Common Service Centre (CSC) / Revenue-Agriculture officer with land records and Aadhaar.
verify_note: Scheme rules, exclusion categories and instalment amounts can change — verify current details on the official portal before applying.

name: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)
short_description: Low-premium crop insurance against yield loss from natural calamities, pests and diseases.
description: A crop insurance scheme where farmers pay a small, uniform share of the premium and the government subsidises the rest, providing a payout when notified crops suffer yield loss due to natural risks such as drought, flood, hailstorm, pest attack or disease.
benefits: Farmers typically pay around 2% of the sum insured for Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi crops, and 5% for annual commercial or horticultural crops; the remaining premium is subsidised by the government. Payout compensates for yield shortfall against a notified threshold.
eligibility: All farmers, including sharecroppers and tenant farmers, growing notified crops in notified areas
Loanee farmers may be enrolled automatically through their bank; other farmers can enrol voluntarily
land_size_info: No minimum or maximum land-size restriction; coverage is per notified crop and area.
irrigation_info: Available regardless of irrigation status; irrigated and rain-fed crops are both covered where notified.
application_process: Apply through your bank (if you have a crop loan), a Common Service Centre, an insurance company agent, or the PMFBY portal, before the season's enrolment cut-off date.
verify_note: The exact list of notified crops, premium rates and cut-off dates changes every season and by state — verify on the official portal.

name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC)
short_description: Short-term credit for crop production and allied farming needs at concessional interest.
description: A credit facility that gives farmers timely access to short-term loans for crop cultivation, post-harvest expenses, and allied activities like animal husbandry and fisheries, through a simplified single-window process at banks.
benefits: Credit at concessional interest rates, with additional interest subvention for prompt repayment. Flexible withdrawal and repayment linked to the cropping cycle.
eligibility: Farmers who own or cultivate land, including tenant farmers, oral lessees and sharecroppers in many states
Members of Self-Help Groups or Joint Liability Groups of farmers
Fisheries and animal husbandry farmers under the extended KCC scheme
land_size_info: No fixed minimum; credit limit is based on land holding, cropping pattern and scale of finance.
irrigation_info: Not a deciding factor; both irrigated and rain-fed farmers can apply.
application_process: Apply at any nationalised bank, cooperative bank or Regional Rural Bank branch with land records or tenancy proof and identity documents.
verify_note: KCC is administered by individual banks under RBI/NABARD guidelines — confirm current interest rates and documentation with your bank.

name: Soil Health Card Scheme
short_description: Free soil testing with crop-wise fertiliser and nutrient recommendations.
description: Under this scheme, farmers' soil samples are tested at government-approved labs and farmers receive a Soil Health Card, typically reissued every 2-3 years, showing nutrient status and the recommended dosage of fertilisers and soil amendments for their farm.
benefits: Free soil testing and a personalised report to help reduce input costs and improve soil productivity over time.
eligibility: Any farmer with agricultural land can request testing through the local agriculture department or Krishi Vigyan Kendra
land_size_info: No restriction; applies to any size of landholding.
irrigation_info: Not a deciding factor for this scheme.
application_process: Contact your local block or district agriculture office, or Krishi Vigyan Kendra, to have a soil sample collected and tested.
verify_note: Testing cycles and lab locations vary by district — confirm with your local agriculture office.

name: PM Krishi Sinchayee Yojana - Per Drop More Crop (Micro-Irrigation)
short_description: Subsidy for drip and sprinkler irrigation systems to improve water-use efficiency.
description: The micro-irrigation component of PMKSY ('Har Khet Ko Pani' — water for every field) provides financial assistance to farmers for installing drip and sprinkler irrigation systems, helping save water and improve yield, especially useful where water availability is limited.
benefits: Combined central and state subsidy that typically covers a large share of the cost of empanelled drip or sprinkler systems, generally higher for small and marginal farmers; several states offer additional top-up support.
eligibility: Farmers with assured access to a water source such as a well, borewell, canal or pond
Priority is often given to small and marginal farmers
land_size_info: Open to all landholding sizes; subsidy percentage may vary by farmer category and state.
irrigation_info: Requires an existing water source to connect the micro-irrigation system to — this scheme upgrades how water is applied, it does not create a new water source.
application_process: Apply through the state Horticulture or Agriculture department portal / district office; installation is done via empanelled vendors and subsidy is released after inspection and geo-tagging.
verify_note: Subsidy percentages and state top-ups vary considerably by state — verify with your state horticulture/agriculture department.

name: PM-KUSUM (Solar Pumps & Solarisation for Farmers)
short_description: Subsidy for solar-powered irrigation pumps and grid-connected solar power for farmers.
description: A Ministry of New and Renewable Energy scheme that helps farmers install standalone solar irrigation pumps and solarise existing grid-connected pumps, reducing diesel or electricity costs, with a component allowing farmers to set up small solar power plants on their land.
benefits: Central and state subsidy on standalone solar pumps (up to 7.5 HP) and on solarising existing electric pumps; a separate component supports setting up small grid-connected solar power plants on farmer, panchayat or FPO land.
eligibility: Individual farmers, groups of farmers, cooperatives, panchayats or FPOs
Availability of suitable land or an existing electric pump connection, depending on which component is applied for
land_size_info: No fixed land-size restriction; requirements depend on the component (standalone pump vs. grid-connected plant) applied for.
irrigation_info: Especially useful for farmers relying on diesel pumps or with unreliable grid electricity for irrigation.
application_process: Apply through your state renewable energy development agency's PM-KUSUM portal, or through your electricity distribution company (DISCOM) for feeder-level solarisation.
verify_note: Component-wise subsidy shares and state allocations change — verify current figures on the official portal.

name: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)
short_description: Support for farmer clusters adopting organic farming.
description: PKVY promotes cluster-based organic farming, providing financial assistance for organic inputs, certification and handholding support to farmer groups that adopt traditional or organic agricultural practices over a multi-year cycle.
benefits: Per-hectare financial assistance for organic inputs, certification costs and value addition, disbursed over a multi-year cluster cycle. Exact amounts vary by scheme guideline year.
eligibility: Farmers willing to form or join a cluster of the minimum required farmers or area
Willingness to transition to organic practices and undergo group certification
land_size_info: No individual land-size restriction, but participation is organised through farmer clusters.
irrigation_info: Not a deciding factor for this scheme.
application_process: Join or form a cluster through your state agriculture department or local Krishi Vigyan Kendra, which coordinates PKVY enrolment.
verify_note: Per-hectare assistance amounts and cluster-size norms are updated periodically — verify with your state agriculture department.

name: Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY)
short_description: Umbrella scheme funding state-level agriculture and allied-sector development projects.
description: RKVY gives states flexibility to plan and fund agriculture and allied-sector projects — infrastructure, value chains, innovation — suited to local needs. Individual farmers and FPOs often benefit indirectly through state-approved sub-schemes and infrastructure built under it.
benefits: Varies by state and project; may include infrastructure support, equipment subsidies, or funding routed through Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs).
eligibility: Eligibility depends on the specific state sub-scheme or project active under RKVY
Often most relevant to farmers who are members of an FPO or cooperative
land_size_info: Depends on the specific state project active under this umbrella scheme.
irrigation_info: Not a fixed criterion; depends on the specific project.
application_process: Check with your state Agriculture Department for currently active RKVY-funded sub-schemes and how to apply.
verify_note: RKVY is implemented very differently in each state — treat this entry as a starting point, not a specific scheme.

name: National Food Security Mission (NFSM)
short_description: Support to boost production of rice, wheat, pulses, coarse cereals and nutri-cereals.
description: NFSM provides farmers with subsidised seeds, cropping-system demonstrations, farm machinery support and training to increase productivity and area coverage of key food-grain crops in identified districts.
benefits: Subsidy on certified or hybrid seeds, farm implements, cropping-system demonstrations, and training, targeted at NFSM-notified districts and crops.
eligibility: Farmers cultivating rice, wheat, pulses, coarse cereals or nutri-cereals in NFSM-notified districts
land_size_info: No fixed restriction; benefits are targeted at notified districts and crops rather than land size.
irrigation_info: Not a deciding factor for this scheme.
application_process: Apply through the district agriculture office; benefits are usually routed through notified district-level programmes.
verify_note: Notified districts and crop list vary by year — verify with your district agriculture office.

name: Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM)
short_description: Subsidy for purchasing farm machinery and setting up Custom Hiring Centres.
description: SMAM helps farmers access modern farm machinery — from tractors and tillers to harvesters — either through a direct purchase subsidy or by promoting Custom Hiring Centres where small farmers can rent equipment affordably instead of buying it.
benefits: Subsidy (percentage varies by equipment, farmer category and state) on eligible farm machinery, plus support for establishing Custom Hiring Centres and Farm Machinery Banks.
eligibility: Individual farmers, FPOs, cooperatives or entrepreneurs setting up Custom Hiring Centres
Higher subsidy rates are often available for small, marginal, SC/ST and women farmers
land_size_info: No fixed land-size restriction; small and marginal farmers often get preferential subsidy rates.
irrigation_info: Not a deciding factor for this scheme.
application_process: Apply through the state agricultural mechanisation portal or district agriculture office; equipment is usually purchased from empanelled dealers.
verify_note: Subsidy percentages differ significantly by state and equipment type — verify current rates before purchase.

name: Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH)
short_description: Support for fruit, vegetable, spice, flower and plantation crop growers.
description: MIDH provides holistic support to horticulture growers, covering planting material, area expansion, protected cultivation such as greenhouses, post-harvest management and marketing infrastructure, to boost horticultural production and farmer income.
benefits: Subsidy on planting material, greenhouses or net houses, drip irrigation combined with horticulture components, and post-harvest infrastructure.
eligibility: Farmers growing or planning to grow horticultural crops such as fruits, vegetables, spices or flowers
land_size_info: No fixed land-size restriction; applies to farmers growing horticultural crops of any scale.
irrigation_info: Not a strict requirement, though many components (like drip irrigation) assume access to a water source.
application_process: Apply through the state Horticulture Department portal or your district horticulture office.
verify_note: Subsidy shares differ by component and state — verify with your state horticulture department.

name: National Beekeeping and Honey Mission (NBHM)
short_description: Support for beekeeping and honey production as a supplementary farm income source.
description: NBHM promotes scientific beekeeping among farmers, providing support for bee colonies, hives, equipment and market linkage, helping farmers earn supplementary income while also improving crop pollination on their farms.
benefits: Subsidy on bee colonies and hive equipment, and support for post-harvest honey infrastructure and market linkages, through implementing agencies such as NAFED and state horticulture or agriculture departments.
eligibility: Farmers or farmer groups interested in taking up beekeeping as a supplementary activity
land_size_info: Not tied to land size — beekeeping can be taken up alongside any cropping pattern.
irrigation_info: Not a deciding factor for this scheme.
application_process: Apply through the state horticulture department or the implementing agency notified for NBHM in your state.
verify_note: Implementing agency and subsidy structure vary by state — confirm locally.

name: Rashtriya Gokul Mission
short_description: Support for indigenous cattle breed conservation and dairy farmers.
description: This scheme supports the conservation and genetic improvement of indigenous cattle breeds, provides access to quality breeding services such as artificial insemination, and works with dairy farmers to improve milk productivity and livelihoods.
benefits: Support for access to artificial insemination, quality breeding bulls, and Gokul Gram breed-improvement centres, indirectly benefiting dairy farmers through better breed availability.
eligibility: Cattle and dairy farmers, especially those rearing indigenous breeds
land_size_info: Not tied to land size — this is a livestock scheme rather than a crop-land scheme.
irrigation_info: Not applicable to this livestock-focused scheme.
application_process: Contact your state Animal Husbandry Department or local veterinary / artificial insemination centre.
verify_note: Programme components and breeding-centre locations vary by state — confirm locally.

name: Livestock Insurance Scheme
short_description: Insurance cover for cattle and other milch or draught animals against death.
description: Provides insurance protection to farmers and cattle rearers against the loss of their livestock due to death from disease, accident or natural calamity, with a subsidised premium.
benefits: Subsidised insurance premium, with higher subsidy in many state implementations for small, marginal or BPL farmers; indemnity is paid on the insured animal's death.
eligibility: Farmers and cattle rearers owning milch or draught animals
land_size_info: Not tied to land size — this is a livestock insurance scheme.
irrigation_info: Not applicable to this livestock-focused scheme.
application_process: Apply through the state Animal Husbandry Department or an empanelled insurance provider.
verify_note: Premium subsidy rates vary by state and animal type — confirm locally.

name: PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME)
short_description: Support to set up or upgrade small food processing units, including farmer groups.
description: PMFME helps existing micro food-processing enterprises, including individual farmers, FPOs and Self-Help Groups doing value addition on farm produce, formalise and upgrade their units with credit-linked subsidy, branding and marketing support.
benefits: Credit-linked capital subsidy (commonly cited around 35% of eligible project cost, subject to a ceiling), support for common infrastructure, and branding or marketing assistance.
eligibility: Existing micro food-processing units, including farmer-run or FPO-run units
Individual entrepreneurs, Self-Help Groups, FPOs and cooperatives
land_size_info: Not tied to land size — relevant to farmers doing value-added food processing on their produce.
irrigation_info: Not a deciding factor for this scheme.
application_process: Apply through the PMFME portal or the district resource person appointed for the scheme.
verify_note: Subsidy ceiling and eligible project costs are revised periodically — verify current figures on the official portal.

name: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF)
short_description: Subsidised loans for post-harvest storage, cold chains and farm-gate infrastructure.
description: AIF provides medium- to long-term debt financing with interest subvention and credit guarantee support for building post-harvest management infrastructure such as warehouses, cold storages and processing units, benefiting farmers, FPOs and agri-entrepreneurs.
benefits: Interest subvention of up to 3% on loans, subject to a ceiling, plus credit guarantee coverage, making infrastructure loans cheaper for eligible borrowers.
eligibility: Individual farmers, FPOs, cooperatives, agri-entrepreneurs and Self-Help Groups setting up eligible post-harvest infrastructure projects
land_size_info: Not tied to land size — relevant to farmers investing in shared or individual post-harvest infrastructure.
irrigation_info: Not a deciding factor for this scheme.
application_process: Apply through the AIF portal; the loan itself is sanctioned by a participating bank or financial institution.
verify_note: Interest subvention ceilings and eligible project types are revised periodically — verify on the official portal.

name: National Bamboo Mission
short_description: Support for farmers taking up bamboo plantation as a crop.
description: Promotes bamboo cultivation on farmland and non-forest areas, supporting farmers with planting material and maintenance assistance, and helping link produce to processing units and markets.
benefits: Financial assistance for bamboo plantation establishment and maintenance over the initial years, subject to scheme norms.
eligibility: Farmers willing to take up bamboo cultivation on their land
land_size_info: No fixed land-size restriction.
irrigation_info: Not a deciding factor for this scheme.
application_process: Apply through the state Forest or Agriculture Department office implementing the National Bamboo Mission.
verify_note: Implementation is state-specific — confirm current assistance amounts locally.

name: e-NAM (National Agriculture Market)
short_description: Online platform for farmers to sell produce with better price discovery across mandis.
description: e-NAM links Agricultural Produce Market Committee (APMC) mandis across states on a single electronic trading platform, allowing farmers to get transparent, competitive price discovery for their produce instead of depending only on the local mandi.
benefits: Access to a wider base of buyers, transparent online bidding, and quicker payment settlement, potentially improving the price farmers receive for their produce.
eligibility: Farmers who can bring produce to, or are linked with, an e-NAM-integrated mandi
land_size_info: No land-size restriction — this is a market-access platform, not a subsidy scheme.
irrigation_info: Not applicable to this market-access scheme.
application_process: Register free of cost at the nearest e-NAM-integrated mandi, or through the e-NAM mobile app.
verify_note: Not all mandis are e-NAM-integrated — confirm whether your nearest mandi participates.

name: Interest Subvention Scheme for Short-Term Crop Loans
short_description: Lower effective interest rate on short-term crop loans repaid on time.
description: Farmers taking short-term crop loans, typically through a Kisan Credit Card, receive an interest subvention that reduces the effective interest rate, with a further prompt-repayment incentive for farmers who repay on schedule.
benefits: Reduced effective interest rate on eligible short-term crop loans up to a notified loan amount, lower still for farmers who repay promptly.
eligibility: Farmers with a short-term crop loan, typically via Kisan Credit Card, up to the notified loan limit
land_size_info: Not tied to land size directly; tied to loan amount instead.
irrigation_info: Not a deciding factor for this scheme.
application_process: Automatically applied by the lending bank on eligible KCC or crop loans — no separate application is usually needed, but confirm with your bank.
verify_note: Notified loan limits and subvention rates are revised periodically — verify with your bank.

name: PM Kisan Maandhan Yojana (PM-KMY)
short_description: Voluntary pension scheme for small and marginal farmers.
description: A voluntary, contributory pension scheme where eligible small and marginal farmers aged 18 to 40 contribute a small monthly amount, matched by the government, into a pension fund, and receive a fixed monthly pension after turning 60.
benefits: Monthly pension after the age of 60, commonly cited as around ₹3,000 per month, with the government matching the farmer's monthly contribution during the accumulation phase.
eligibility: Small and marginal farmers with landholding up to 2 hectares (about 5 acres), aged 18 to 40
Should not already be covered under another statutory pension scheme or be an income-tax payer
land_size_info: Restricted to small and marginal farmers holding up to about 5 acres (2 hectares).
irrigation_info: Not a deciding factor for this scheme.
application_process: Enrol at the nearest Common Service Centre with Aadhaar and bank account details, or self-enrol via the PM-KMY portal.
verify_note: Pension amount and contribution slabs are fixed by scheme rules — verify current figures before enrolling.

name: Micro irrigation Fund
short_description: The Micro Irrigation Fund (MIF), established under NABARD in 2019-20 with an initial corpus of Rs. 5,000 crore and augmented by another Rs. 5,000 crore in 20...
description: The Micro Irrigation Fund (MIF), established under NABARD in 2019-20 with an initial corpus of Rs. 5,000 crore and augmented by another Rs. 5,000 crore in 2024, is a government initiative aimed at promoting the adoption of micro irrigation systems such as drip and sprinkler technologies to enhance water-use efficiency and agricultural productivity in India, offering states low-interest loans with a 2% interest subvention to provide farmer subsidies beyond existing PMKSY provisions, with small and marginal farmers receiving a 55% central subsidy and others 45%, supplemented by three years of free maintenance services, facilitating water conservation, improved soil health, labor and power savings, and increased crop yield across states like Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, and Rajasthan, while enabling innovative irrigation projects, public-private partnerships, and sustainable agriculture development, with farmers applying through FPOs, cooperatives, Water User Associations, or state agencies, making MIF a strategic financial tool for widespread sustainable irrigation adoption.
application_process: See the official scheme website for the current application process.
verify_note: Added via the plain-text admin form — verify current details on the official website before relying on this scheme.
